A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HOLLM and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Earlier experiments and analyses can be matched to their relocated counterparts in v2, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original optimization experiments on synthetic functions, FCNet, and NAS-Bench-201, together with sampling demonstrations and component and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and reports additional simulator, observation-noise, and LLM-choice experiments. This judgment does not depend on the calibration results explicitly attributed to follow-up work in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The five-stage algorithm and scoring equations remain intact. Algorithm 3 revises the documented empty-cell branch from assigning mu=0 and expl=1 to assigning mu,V,E=0,1,1. Listing 3 also adds an explicit pre-output constraint-check instruction. These are localized procedural revisions.

E1.justification: V2 adds Penicillin Production, Vehicle Safety, and Car Side Impact simulator tasks, plus a noisy Vehicle Safety scenario. The original six synthetic functions, four FCNet datasets, and NAS-Bench-201 tasks remain represented; Ackley and NAS results move to Appendix C.1 rather than disappearing.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds LA-MCTS variants, CMA-ES, HEBO, and SMAC comparisons; Appendix F adds TabPFN and a distinct GP ranking-surrogate comparison. RS + KD-Tree expands from a v1 component ablation into main benchmark comparisons. The new main synthetic plots omit TPE and TuRBO, whose earlier comparisons remain in Appendix C.1.

E3.justification: The default LLM changes from Gemini-1.5-Flash to Gemini-2.0-Flash, and the reported default budget changes from T=100 to T=50. V2 also introduces longer-budget baseline comparisons, Gaussian observation noise with standard deviation 1% of the objective range, and diversity and surrogate-evaluation protocols, including a reported 700-point calibration analysis. Earlier settings remain documented separately.

E4.justification: V2 adds Vehicle Safety scoring ablations, observation-noise robustness, comparisons across open-weight LLMs, and sampling-diversity analysis. Appendix F examines surrogate ranking and calibration while retaining the LLM candidate sampler, explicitly attributing those results to follow-up work. Earlier NAS component ablations and hyperparameter analyses are retained, with additional Gemini-2.0 exploration-weight results.

E5.justification: The revised main evaluation reports 10 runs instead of v1's default 3, while retained appendix experiments preserve their earlier counts. V2 adds a critical-difference rank diagram and reports five repetitions for Table 4. Mean and standard-error reporting continues; the diagram's statistical test and significance level are not specified.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive benchmark and analysis results while retaining earlier curves. Its new Gemini-2.0 Figure 3 shows the global LLM outperforming HOLLM on Rastrigin under the revised settings. New Table 4 reports Rosenbrock scores of -7.03 ± 0.01 for HOLLM and -4.66 ± 0.50 for the global LLM. These additions do not establish same-setting performance changes relative to v1.

T1.justification: Appendix D introduces a mathematical definition of ICL Divergence as mean nearest-context-point distance. Appendix G adds an asymptotic complexity comparison between HOLLM, global LLM sampling, and exact GP methods. The original scoring mathematics is retained, and neither version supplies regret guarantees.

C1.justification: The central contribution—improving LLM optimization through adaptive partitioning and bandit-inspired selection—remains unchanged. The introduction and conclusion replace their emphasis on NAS with claims of applicability to real-world optimization tasks, and the abstract describes comparisons against leading global optimization methods more generally.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands explanations of variance-aware scoring, sampling collapse, global-history conditioning, surrogate behavior, and computational scaling. Its FCNet discussion emphasizes discrete-space and model-dependent effects instead of v1's Parkinsons outlier hypothesis. It also qualifies the retained three-run synthetic evidence as needing more repetitions and discusses differing benefits across continuous and discrete domains.

D1.justification: V2 adds simulator parameter ranges, surrogate prediction choices, and an approximate FCNet runtime and API cost of 330 seconds and $0.14 per 50-trial run. It clarifies global-history conditioning, updates prompt instructions, and changes the code pointer from automl/hollm to arberzela/mohollm. Much of the existing pseudocode, hyperparameter documentation, and prompt material is retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting the new optimizers, simulator suite, Llama/Qwen models, TabPFN, and follow-up multi-objective HOLLM work. The main related-work discussion and positioning relative to hierarchical bandits, Bayesian optimization, and LLM optimizers remain largely unchanged. The citation-style conversion itself is presentational.

P1.justification: The evaluation narrative and appendix organization are substantially reworked. NAS becomes Appendix C.1.3, the main text gains dedicated real-world and analysis sections, and prompts move from Appendix D to I around newly organized analyses. Several experimental interpretations are rewritten, alongside conference-format, affiliation, and acknowledgment edits.

P2.justification: V2 adds engineering-task plots, a critical-difference diagram, robustness and model-choice panels, diversity and calibration visualizations, and comparison and complexity tables. Main synthetic results change from a six-panel grid to a five-panel strip with a shared legend, while earlier plots are retained in the appendices. Figure arrangements and the document-wide conference layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical validation through simulator tasks, competing partitioning methods, more main-evaluation repetitions, and tests of noise and LLM dependence, addressing important gaps in v1's evidence while retaining its experiments. Some claims remain too broad: Table 4 does not establish universal HOLLM superiority, and the critical-difference procedure is underspecified. These weaknesses temper the conclusions but do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and understanding.
